# Attribution and evidence boundaries

Prepared for Vladimir Reshetnikov's ProveIt research program, 24 October 2026.
This research, code and exposition were prepared with AI assistance. Separately
tasked research-agent reviews are internal reviews within this workflow, not
external human peer review, institutional endorsement or formal-kernel proofs.

New material is offered under ProveIt's MIT No Attribution license. Imported
material retains its original notices and licenses; the top-level license does
not relicense third-party material.

The graph normalization, equality cycles and unit path adapt the incoming
Height One and Degree 464 packet. The new graph-incidence architecture, shared
factors and C4-free factor reuse preserve the literal source zero sets. The
source442 and source519 calibrations remain identified inherited ordinary
theorems. The direct branch combines the credited incoming modular-binomial
and one-cap Pell constructions, with new compatibility and signed-recovery
proofs. The eleven-variable branch has its separate native/source34/K215
calibration and retains the full fixed numeral tuple.

The public comparison boundary is the full commit and eight archives recorded
in provenance/REPOSITORY_SNAPSHOT.json. New measurements are exact finite
properties of the delivered objects. No global simplicity minimum,
literature-wide priority claim, proof of Con(ZFC), or newly completed
end-to-end Lean/Rocq/object-language ZFC certificate is asserted.
